# PIXL/1 normative specification

Status: implemented version 1.0.0. PIXL is a project-specific, agent-operated UDL; this document is its decoder contract. The wire form has no human usability requirement. Host profiles are a separate translating layer. Reserved notation cannot silently acquire a new meaning.

## Wire grammar

Input is UTF-8, maximum 16 MiB. ASCII whitespace is insignificant outside literals. There are no comments, escapes, implicit coercions, expressions, interpolation, executable imports, or indentation semantics. Parsing is bounded to 64 nested value containers and 100,000 records. ASCII identifiers match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,95}`. IDs are case sensitive and document-unique.

```ebnf
document = "PX1", whitespace, revision, whitespace, { record, whitespace } ;
record   = "@", identifier, ":", kind, map ;
map      = "{", [ identifier, "=", value, { ";", identifier, "=", value } ], "}" ;
list     = "[", [ value, { ",", value } ], "]" ;
value    = literal | reference | symbol | integer | list | map | "+" | "-" | "?" ;
reference= "@", identifier ;
symbol   = identifier ;
integer  = [ "-" ], digit, { digit } ;
literal  = "~", unsigned-byte-count, ":", exactly-that-many-UTF8-bytes ;
kind     = one-uppercase-ASCII-letter ;
revision = unsigned-integer ;
```

`+` is true, `-` is false, `?` is absent/null. Integers are signed 64-bit; lengths and revisions are nonnegative. Floating-point wire values are intentionally absent: coordinates are integer pixels; duration is integer milliseconds; fractional quantities use declared fixed-point units in asset metadata, or opaque provider JSON at the boundary. A symbol and a literal with the same visible text are different values. A reference is never a string. Lengths count UTF-8 bytes, not characters. `~0:` is an empty literal. A literal may contain newlines, delimiters, backslashes or NUL without acquiring syntax. A malformed UTF-8 length boundary is an error. Duplicate fields are errors.

Canonical encoding starts `PX1 <revision>\n`, sorts records by ID and map fields by ASCII key, preserves list order, uses decimal integers without leading zeroes and one newline after each record. Canonical map/list values contain no insignificant whitespace. SHA-256 over canonical document bytes is the snapshot identity. SHA-256 over the canonical record bytes (without the trailing newline) is a record identity. Revision is not a record field. Noncanonical valid input can be normalized without changing its semantic values.

## Semantic registry

The complete field/type dictionary is [`registry.json`](../pixl/registry.json). That machine-readable registry and this specification are normative together. Unknown kinds, fields and closed-enum values fail validation; extension requires a new explicit version. All fields are required unless marked optional in the registry. `tg` is an optional list of literal tags on every kind. Map payloads are permitted only in declared fields; they cannot override core fields.

The bundled operational knowledge library is `knowledge/library.px`. Its K `rq` prerequisites and `rk` failure conditions preserve the curated source conditions. `ap` atoms are generated from source applicability phrases with stable SHA-256 suffixes; their exact meanings are in the hash-bound `knowledge/applicability.json` source. They are domain symbols, not inferred new core language rules. Source JSON is retained for curation and host interchange; the compiled K/S/E graph is available directly to contextual operation.

| Kind | Meaning | Operational replacement |
|---|---|---|
| A | actor and responsibility | ownership / agent role |
| P | project and active visual contract | project design envelope |
| S | source with digest and locator | reference tagging / provenance |
| R | runtime/tool dependency with exact version locator | tech stack |
| C | visual contract, dimensions, palette, view, sampling and alpha policy | art design document |
| K | applicable knowledge method, procedure, checks, research and POC references | technical knowledge |
| D | decision: `wh` who, `wt` what, `wr` where, `wy` why, `rs` research, `pc` proof | design rationale |
| T | task, ownership, dependencies, decisions, inputs/outputs, state and evidence | work plan / TODO / dependency graph |
| X | artifact/reference and its expected bytes, contract and metadata | asset manifest / content map |
| E | evidence receipt, outcome, mode, file hash and bound record hashes | test/review result |
| J | external job identity, request digest and observed state | tool execution memory |
| N | resumption focus, next tasks and blockers at a specific revision | contextual handoff |

References resolve within the document and must match the declared target kind. Task `dp` edges are directed from dependent to prerequisite and must be acyclic. Other reference cycles are legal (for example a decision and its proof) and closure uses visited IDs. Ready tasks are open tasks whose prerequisites are all done. Dropped prerequisites do not satisfy a dependency. Active/blocked/done tasks are not advertised as ready. A done task needs at least one current passing evidence receipt and all prerequisites done; those passing receipts must collectively bind every current `io` artifact record. A task cannot be done with no `io` artifact. Evidence binding `{rf=@id;dg=~64:<record-sha256>}` snapshots the full record, not its name. Any record change invalidates that binding. Passing evidence does not erase failing evidence.

Decisions require nonempty research and proof lists, and nonempty who/what/where/why content. Their current proof receipts must collectively bind the decision record itself and its semantic dependency closure. Proof receipts may report failure: a decision can reject a failed method. A K with `pc` must have current receipts binding that method and its semantic sources; an active/done task requires passing receipts covering that scope. K methods without executed proof are retained as researched knowledge, but an agent must execute an applicable POC before adoption. A method's recipe is not an executed proof. Agents preserve conflicting observations in separate source/evidence records and resolve them through a new decision rather than overwriting history.

**Semantic proof scope** traverses only `A/S/R/C/K/D/X`. It stops before workflow/project/proof kinds `P/E/T/J/N`, which would otherwise entangle mutable task states and proof history with the result being proved. X proof bindings must cover its scope, including the linked C. Link source/runtime/contract records directly when their content is part of the proof; a pointer through P does not bind that project's contents. K and D can point to E by ID while E binds their hash: the hash contains reference IDs, not recursive target hashes.

Evidence `ob=+` marks a superseded receipt. Its original outcome, file and old bindings remain preserved; outdated record hashes are allowed only in superseded receipts. Such receipts never count for decisions, method adoption or completion. Store commits forbid modifying existing E fields except one-way supersession; add a new E ID for new execution. Receipt metadata is a caller assertion supported by retained files. Hash validation establishes identity and freshness, not cryptographic attestation that a model, service or test runner told the truth.

File checking is optional for structural validation and mandatory when accepting completion in a store. With a project root, X/E local paths and locally addressed S bytes must exist, remain within that root after symlink resolution, and match their declared SHA-256. URL sources are not downloaded by validation; their digest identifies a recorded snapshot and does not assert current remote truth. Source `ln` ranges are inclusive, one-based and valid for the local source. Empty palettes mean no exact palette restriction, not zero colors. C rules apply only to linked artifacts; source art can intentionally choose a different contract.

## Retrieval and drift

`context(focus)` includes the focus, all project roots and their transitive references, and the focus's transitive reference closure. For T focus it also includes associated J records and handoffs mentioning the focus. This is a conservative correctness baseline; it never silently truncates a required dependency or decision. If canonical packet bytes exceed a requested byte budget it returns a budget error with the required size. Bytes are not claimed to equal model tokens. Large project roots should not reference every task: tasks point to their project. Returned subsets keep the original revision and validate as closed documents.

`impact(id)` traverses reverse references transitively. The changed node itself is included. `ready` returns stable sorted task IDs. A content map is a query over X/S records and `tg`; a stack is a query over R; decisions over D. There are no duplicated authoritative Markdown TODO/stack state files. Source catalogs are derived indexes and can be rebuilt.

## State publication

A store contains `state.px`, immutable `history/<canonical-sha>.px`, and a temporary exclusive `.lock` while writing. Initialize once. A candidate must have exactly current revision + 1; caller must supply the current canonical hash. Under the lock, reload current state, compare revision/hash, validate the complete candidate and its files, write/fsync its history snapshot and a same-directory temporary state, then atomically replace state. The final state is the commit point. A crash may leave an unreferenced valid history snapshot or lock; it must not publish a partial document. A leftover lock fails with recovery guidance; it is never automatically broken while a writer might be alive. Filesystem snapshots provide local recovery, not distributed consensus or protection from a malicious filesystem writer. Direct manual state editing bypasses these guarantees and is unsupported for operation.

Task transitions: open -> active/blocked/dropped; active -> blocked/done/dropped; blocked -> open/active/dropped; done -> open; dropped -> open. Unchanged states are allowed. Existing IDs cannot disappear or change kind during commit; close/drop records instead. Any change to a done task or its complete reference closure requires reopening that task. Supersede invalidated receipts with `ob=+`, retain their original bindings, add new receipt IDs after new execution, and redirect D/K/T evidence references deliberately. Revision increases are mandatory even for resumption changes.

C describes raster dimensions and rendering intent. X of kind `code` or `report` associates with its production contract but is not interpreted as a raster image. X metadata is an opaque declared payload: the core validates wire values and references, not a target engine's atlas/rig schema. Domain knowledge recipes and appropriate project tools validate those additional contracts. A structural/file validation alone does not establish visual acceptance.

## PixelLab boundary

The host retrieves the actual connected PixelLab tool input schema. PIXL prepares a validated intent with exact tool name, arguments, schema digest and request digest. JSON here is the MCP provider's interchange, not PIXL syntax. Preparation has no remote side effect. The host calls the provider and journals the observed real ID. Generation starts prepared -> submitted -> running -> succeeded/failed; submitted/running may become unknown when observation is lost. Unknown is not permission to recreate a paid job. Recovery requires observation of the existing job; there is no automatic generation retry. A generation result is an artifact candidate, not proof of quality or task completion.

Durations/credits reported in research are estimates from a dated documentation snapshot. Discovered schemas take precedence over snapshots. PixelLab credentials remain in host secret configuration. This runtime does not impersonate PixelLab or invent job IDs. Its MCP server exposes local project tools only; the host connects the actual PixelLab MCP separately.

## Verification boundaries

The suite verifies parsing, graph invariants, writes, request validation, job transitions, artifact measurements, deterministic method POCs and local MCP behavior. Image inspection hashes and measures one immutable in-memory byte snapshot, checks every frame's dimensions and cumulative pixel limit, and labels visual/engine acceptance unverified. Token measurements are encoding-specific comparisons with the same semantic payload, including bootstrap overhead separately. They are not a controlled LLM capability or artistic-quality study. A full live PixelLab job and target-engine visual acceptance must be recorded with real evidence before those outcomes are asserted.

# Observation of reference.png

Recorded 2026-09-11 by PIXL. File: `reference.png` in the project root.
SHA-256 of the file bytes: `d997cadefc6b94c1c14f4ec17159deaf5ceb7ea9543b2522390ea1a577470aa7`.

## Measured (pixl_asset_check plus Pillow color census)

- Mode RGBA, single frame, 32 x 32 pixels.
- 390 pixels with nonzero alpha; 634 fully transparent pixels.
- 0 pixels with fractional alpha. Alpha values present are exactly 0 and 255.
- 3 distinct visible colors.
- 1 opaque connected component under 4-connectivity.
- Visible bounding box (x0, y0, x1, y1) = (7, 3, 25, 28); the art is inset from every edge.

### Exact palette with pixel counts

| Hex | RGBA | Visible pixels | Role read from the image |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `#25354A` | (37, 53, 74, 255) | 180 | Dark outline and antennae |
| `#56B5BC` | (86, 181, 188, 255) | 186 | Teal body fill |
| `#F4DDA2` | (244, 221, 162, 255) | 24 | Pale-yellow eyes (two 2x3 blocks, 12 px each) |

There is no fourth color, so the reference offers no shading ramp and no separate
highlight or antenna color.

## Visually inspected at 12x nearest-neighbor enlargement (`work/reference_x12.png`)

The reference is a schematic color-and-feature key rather than a finished character:

- A single rectangular body with a uniform two-pixel dark outline on all sides, filled flat
  teal. No interior shading, no dithering, no anti-aliasing.
- Two straight vertical antennae rising from the top edge, drawn in the outline color only,
  one near each top corner, separated by a transparent gap.
- Two pale-yellow rectangular eyes on the upper body, evenly spaced, with no pupil and no
  outline of their own.
- No ground shadow, no ground contact cluster, and no detached pixels anywhere.
- The face reads frontally because both eyes sit on the same visible plane and the form is
  bilaterally symmetric. The reference does not itself demonstrate a side view.

## Consequences for the sample

- The palette constraint is exactly three opaque colors. This is the tightest constraint in
  the brief and the one most likely to be missed by a generator.
- Binary alpha and "no ground shadow" are both already true of the reference and are
  directly measurable on a candidate.
- "Side view" comes from the owner's text, not from this image; the image only supplies
  palette, feature inventory, outline weight and flat-fill treatment.

1	# Provider submission and recovery operation
2	
3	Use this operation when a PIXL production task needs an external generation request, a submitted attempt needs resumption, or a returned candidate needs to enter project state. Developing this operation is a maintainer task; only a production assignment or explicit evaluation activates PIXL.
4	
5	Read the [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md), its [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json), and the [journal contract](../../../resources/spec/provider-recovery.md). This operation uses the explicit J.jr/op/xs extension. Existing unjournaled J and PX1 stores keep their earlier meanings; adding fields or changing a header does not manufacture durable history.
6	
7	## Required context
8	
9	- The project root, current store state/hash, task and selected planned F outputs. Use the [intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md) first if choices or criteria are missing. Sample tasks may test proposals; dependent production still needs adoption and confirmation.
10	- The actual connected provider identity, selected tool and exact inputSchema observed through this harness, with a retained discovery source, timestamp and evidence. A cached capabilities list is advisory. If live tools are absent, preserve the plan and explain the missing capability; do not invent a discovery observation.
11	- The user's established authorized scope and budget, retained as a scope string and evidence object. Existing authorization can support this record; a local tool does not grant new authority. Resolve a consequential missing budget/permission before a paid call while continuing independent work.
12	- For recovery, the saved intent and every retained observation. For import, the actual already downloaded file and evidence relating it to this returned resource. Keep credentials out of arguments, schema examples, discovery, authorization and response evidence.
13	
14	Resolve `../../../scripts/pixl.py` relative to this reference directory and invoke its absolute path using the selected Python environment. The commands below omit that common prefix. Use the same project `--root ROOT` throughout; STORE is a subdirectory of ROOT. Every mutation consumes the current `--expect HASH` and returns the next hash. Files and evidence belong in the project, outside installed resources.
15	
16	## Prepare a saved request
17	
18	1. Run `workflow STORE/state.px --root ROOT` and `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. Read both lifecycle blockers and existing provider attempts. An open task does not imply permission to create another remote job. Pending prepared/unknown/submitted/running work on the output must be resolved first.
19	2. Retrieve the task's focused context. Translate its intended output and relevant inputs, decisions, methods and contract into the actual tool schema. Preserve arguments exactly; describe any requirement the tool cannot express and the later acceptance check that will evaluate it.
20	3. Write a request JSON object with exactly `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `discovery`, and `authorization`. `schema` is the full inputSchema object. Discovery has `source`, `observed_at`, `evidence`; authorization has `scope`, `evidence`. Evidence must be nonempty objects. Timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and at most six fractional digits. Values come from the current assignment and observations, not from a bundled art fixture.
21	4. Run `job-prepare STORE JOB TASK REQUEST_JSON --outputs OUTPUT ... --expect HASH --root ROOT`. This saves exact request/schema/provenance/authorization and the relevant plan hashes. Read its cached assessment: a conflict is a reason to inspect current documentation and tool semantics, not to silently rewrite the request or substitute the cache for the observed schema. Schema validity alone cannot establish account entitlement, output quality or actual cost.
22	
23	Preparation is complete when state contains the prepared J and immutable journal X/E. No remote action has occurred. A missing tool, unresolved project requirement or missing authorization leaves useful local planning intact.
24	
25	## Claim once, then call the actual provider
26	
27	Run `job-dispatch STORE JOB --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Only a successful publication returns `dispatch_request`. It first records a local dispatch claim and moves the saved job to **unknown**, before the host sends anything. Use exactly the returned provider/tool/arguments for the one authorized host call. Do not add defaults or replace arguments after claiming; that would be a different request.
28	
29	The local command does not submit, poll, authenticate or download. `remote_executed: false` describes the local tool even when its journal later records a caller-observed success. Real provider effects remain the host's responsibility.
30	
31	Retain the response without credentials and use `job-observe STORE JOB STATE EVIDENCE_JSON --remote-id RETURNED_ID --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Accepted states submitted/running/succeeded require the actual observed identifier. A supplied failure can be recorded without inventing an ID. After identity is known, omitting `--remote-id` preserves it; it cannot be rebound. Repeat running/unknown observations only when supported by actual observations. A failed or succeeded outcome is terminal for observations.
32	
33	If submission returns no usable answer, record `unknown` with the actual timeout/transport evidence when available. Never treat the initial unknown claim as evidence that a provider received the request, and never treat a missing ID as evidence that it did not.
34	
35	## Resume and reconcile
36	
37	Start with `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. It returns the saved request, context, event history, remote identity, candidate associations, drift and next action. Reading a request is not a new dispatch grant.
38	
39	| Saved state / issue | Next operation |
40	|---|---|
41	| Prepared, context current, no blockers | Claim with job-dispatch before one host call |
42	| Prepared, plan drift or lifecycle blocker | Resolve the specific context; abandon obsolete intent with an evidenced failed observation if appropriate, then prepare a new request ID |
43	| Unknown | Reconcile using the actual provider's documented lookup/status capabilities and retained evidence; do not dispatch or recreate |
44	| Submitted/running with ID | Inspect that exact resource using its discovered status tool, then record the observed response |
45	| Succeeded | Retrieve the actual output through the host, import local candidate bytes, then evaluate acceptance |
46	| Failed | Preserve failure, establish its consequence and any still-valid retry authorization, then use a new job ID for a new attempt |
47	| Legacy unjournaled job | Inspect its actual available history manually; do not attach a fictional journal or ignore pending work |
48	| File/hash error | Preserve the diagnostic and restore the exact retained bytes from available history/backups before continuing; do not rewrite receipts to make a changed file pass |
49	
50	A crash between claim and host submission also leaves unknown. If no provider lookup can resolve whether the request was sent, leave that uncertainty explicit and continue independent work. Elapsed time cannot authorize a retry. A confirmed non-acceptance or terminal failure may support a failed observation and a newly authorized attempt; record that evidence first. Automatic remote exactly-once delivery is not claimed.
51	
52	On `stale_write` or `store_locked`, no dispatch grant was returned. Reread the state and owner information, then reconcile the attempted local change. Do not blindly repeat job-dispatch if another writer already claimed it. Immutable blobs left by a failed publication are unreferenced preparation data; state.px is the publication authority.
53	
54	## Import and hand back to acceptance
55	
56	Download with the actual host/provider mechanism into the project. Then run `job-import STORE JOB OUTPUT CANDIDATE DOWNLOADED_PATH EVIDENCE_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT`. DOWNLOADED_PATH is relative to ROOT. This copies a byte snapshot into the store and creates X.of for the original F, plus a retained import event and J.xs reference. It preserves the downloaded original. It does not nominate the candidate, measure the image, grant V, or finish T.
57	
58	Import rejects changed output/contract/criterion context. Keep the returned file and original history; reconcile the intended plan explicitly before associating it. A new interpretation must not relabel an old generation as though it used the new contract. Submitted observations can still be recorded while the plan has drifted.
59	
60	Retrieve the imported X to obtain its retained path/hash. Run relevant mechanical inspection, review the actual image at native and enlarged scale, and exercise the required destination checks. Follow the [intake/sample acceptance procedure](intake-sample.md) to nominate a candidate deliberately and record each Q's pass, fail or unavailable verdict. Provider success and journal-retention receipts cannot satisfy those requirements.
61	
62	The operation stops with a truthful recovery action or an imported candidate ready for its specified acceptance checks. Handoff includes the job and candidate IDs, actual observed state, retained paths, unresolved checks and the next dependency. No finished asset family or engine readiness follows from this local operation alone.
63

"""Acceptance harness for the teal scout robot sample.

Runs the locally decidable criteria declared in .pixl/state.px against a candidate PNG
and writes a JSON receipt plus a contact sheet for the visual criterion.

    python tools/check_sprite.py CANDIDATE.png --out work/receipt.json \
        --sheet work/contact-sheet.png

Criteria implemented here:
  q.canvas   mechanical  single 32x32 frame
  q.palette  mechanical  zero pixels outside #25354A / #56B5BC / #F4DDA2
  q.alpha    mechanical  zero fractional-alpha pixels
  q.nearest  other       8x nearest enlargement adds no colour and tiles uniformly

q.identity (visual) and q.webdisplay (engine) are NOT decided here. This script only
renders the contact sheet an agent or person must actually look at, and reports the
measurements that support -- but cannot replace -- that judgement.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import pathlib
import sys
from collections import Counter

from PIL import Image

PALETTE = ["#25354A", "#56B5BC", "#F4DDA2"]
SIZE = (32, 32)
ZOOM = 8


def rgba(hex_color):
    value = hex_color.lstrip("#")
    return tuple(int(value[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4)) + (255,)


ALLOWED = {rgba(c) for c in PALETTE}


def load_frames(path):
    with Image.open(path) as image:
        count = getattr(image, "n_frames", 1)
        frames = []
        for index in range(count):
            image.seek(index)
            frames.append(image.convert("RGBA").copy())
    return frames


def visible(frame):
    return [p for p in frame.getdata() if p[3] != 0]


def check_canvas(frames):
    sizes = [f.size for f in frames]
    ok = len(frames) == 1 and sizes[0] == SIZE
    return ok, {"frame_count": len(frames), "sizes": [list(s) for s in sizes],
                "required": [list(SIZE), "single frame"]}


def check_palette(frame):
    counts = Counter(visible(frame))
    outside = sorted(c for c in counts if c not in ALLOWED)
    ok = not outside
    return ok, {
        "visible_colors": len(counts),
        "outside_palette_count": len(outside),
        "outside_palette": ["#%02X%02X%02X (alpha %d)" % (c[0], c[1], c[2], c[3])
                            for c in outside[:16]],
        "counts": {"#%02X%02X%02X" % c[:3]: n for c, n in counts.most_common()},
    }


def check_alpha(frame):
    alphas = Counter(p[3] for p in frame.getdata())
    fractional = sum(n for a, n in alphas.items() if a not in (0, 255))
    return fractional == 0, {"fractional_alpha_pixels": fractional,
                             "alpha_levels": sorted(alphas)}


def check_nearest(frame, zoom=ZOOM):
    """Integer nearest enlargement must add no colour and tile uniformly."""
    big = frame.resize((frame.width * zoom, frame.height * zoom), Image.NEAREST)
    source_colors = set(frame.getdata())
    new_colors = sorted(set(big.getdata()) - source_colors)
    ragged = []
    for y in range(frame.height):
        for x in range(frame.width):
            block = big.crop((x * zoom, y * zoom, (x + 1) * zoom, (y + 1) * zoom))
            distinct = set(block.getdata())
            if len(distinct) != 1 or distinct.pop() != frame.getpixel((x, y)):
                ragged.append([x, y])
    ok = not new_colors and not ragged
    return ok, {"zoom": zoom, "new_colors": len(new_colors),
                "nonuniform_blocks": len(ragged), "first_nonuniform": ragged[:8]}


def checkerboard(size, cell=8):
    board = Image.new("RGBA", size, (255, 255, 255, 255))
    for y in range(0, size[1], cell):
        for x in range(0, size[0], cell):
            if (x // cell + y // cell) % 2:
                board.paste((203, 203, 203, 255), (x, y, min(x + cell, size[0]),
                                                   min(y + cell, size[1])))
    return board


def contact_sheet(candidate, reference, path):
    """Reference and candidate at 8x over light, dark and checker backgrounds,
    plus both at native 32x32, in one image to be looked at."""
    pad, zoom = 8, ZOOM
    tile = 32 * zoom
    backgrounds = [("light", (245, 245, 245, 255)), ("dark", (18, 18, 18, 255)),
                   ("checker", None)]
    cols, rows = 2, len(backgrounds)
    width = pad + cols * (tile + pad)
    height = pad + rows * (tile + pad) + 32 + pad * 2
    sheet = Image.new("RGBA", (width, height), (128, 128, 128, 255))
    for row, (_, color) in enumerate(backgrounds):
        y = pad + row * (tile + pad)
        for col, image in enumerate((reference, candidate)):
            x = pad + col * (tile + pad)
            back = (checkerboard((tile, tile)) if color is None
                    else Image.new("RGBA", (tile, tile), color))
            back.alpha_composite(image.resize((tile, tile), Image.NEAREST))
            sheet.paste(back, (x, y))
    y = pad + rows * (tile + pad)
    for col, image in enumerate((reference, candidate)):
        back = Image.new("RGBA", (32, 32), (245, 245, 245, 255))
        back.alpha_composite(image)
        sheet.paste(back, (pad + col * (tile + pad), y))
    sheet.save(path)
    return path


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("candidate")
    parser.add_argument("--reference", default="reference.png")
    parser.add_argument("--out")
    parser.add_argument("--sheet")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    frames = load_frames(args.candidate)
    frame = frames[0]
    results = {}
    results["q.canvas"] = check_canvas(frames)
    results["q.palette"] = check_palette(frame)
    results["q.alpha"] = check_alpha(frame)
    results["q.nearest"] = check_nearest(frame)

    receipt = {
        "candidate": args.candidate,
        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(args.candidate).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        "contract": {"px": list(SIZE), "pl": PALETTE, "al": "binary", "sa": "nearest"},
        "criteria": {k: {"outcome": "pass" if ok else "fail", "measurements": data}
                     for k, (ok, data) in results.items()},
        "not_decided_here": {
            "q.identity": "visual criterion; requires actually viewing the contact sheet",
            "q.webdisplay": "engine criterion; requires the owner's web prototype",
        },
    }
    if args.sheet:
        reference = load_frames(args.reference)[0]
        receipt["contact_sheet"] = contact_sheet(frame, reference, args.sheet)
    text = json.dumps(receipt, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    if args.out:
        pathlib.Path(args.out).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    print(text)
    return 0 if all(ok for ok, _ in results.values()) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Proof of concept for the acceptance harness itself, before any candidate exists.

Question: do the locally decidable criteria (q.canvas, q.palette, q.alpha, q.nearest)
actually discriminate, or would they pass anything?

Method: run tools/check_sprite.py's checks on a positive control (reference.png, which
satisfies the mechanical half of the contract) and on four mutants, each breaking exactly
one criterion. Acceptance, stated before running: the control passes all four; each mutant
fails exactly its own criterion and no other.
"""
import json
import pathlib
import sys

from PIL import Image

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "tools"))
import check_sprite as cs  # noqa: E402

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "work" / "poc"
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

base = cs.load_frames(ROOT / "reference.png")[0]


def mutate_palette(img):
    """One body pixel shifted by a single blue step: #56B5BC -> #56B5BD."""
    img = img.copy()
    for y in range(img.height):
        for x in range(img.width):
            if img.getpixel((x, y)) == (86, 181, 188, 255):
                img.putpixel((x, y), (86, 181, 189, 255))
                return img
    raise AssertionError("no body pixel found")


def mutate_alpha(img):
    """One body pixel given a half-transparent alpha."""
    img = img.copy()
    for y in range(img.height):
        for x in range(img.width):
            p = img.getpixel((x, y))
            if p == (86, 181, 188, 255):
                img.putpixel((x, y), (86, 181, 188, 128))
                return img
    raise AssertionError("no body pixel found")


def mutate_canvas(img):
    """Delivered one pixel too wide."""
    grown = Image.new("RGBA", (img.width + 1, img.height), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    grown.paste(img, (0, 0))
    return grown


CASES = [
    ("control", base, set()),
    ("mutant-palette", mutate_palette(base), {"q.palette"}),
    ("mutant-alpha", mutate_alpha(base), {"q.alpha"}),
    ("mutant-canvas", mutate_canvas(base), {"q.canvas"}),
]

report = {"question": __doc__.strip().splitlines()[2].strip(), "cases": []}
ok_overall = True

for name, image, expected_failures in CASES:
    path = OUT / f"{name}.png"
    image.save(path)
    frames = cs.load_frames(path)
    frame = frames[0]
    outcomes = {
        "q.canvas": cs.check_canvas(frames),
        "q.palette": cs.check_palette(frame),
        "q.alpha": cs.check_alpha(frame),
        "q.nearest": cs.check_nearest(frame),
    }
    failed = {k for k, (ok, _) in outcomes.items() if not ok}
    agrees = failed == expected_failures
    ok_overall &= agrees
    report["cases"].append({
        "name": name, "path": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/"),
        "expected_failures": sorted(expected_failures),
        "actual_failures": sorted(failed),
        "as_predicted": agrees,
        "measurements": {k: data for k, (_, data) in outcomes.items()},
    })

# Negative control for the sampling mode itself: the same 32x32 art enlarged with a
# smoothing filter must fail the uniform-block condition that nearest enlargement passes.
big_bilinear = base.resize((base.width * cs.ZOOM, base.height * cs.ZOOM), Image.BILINEAR)
source_colors = set(base.getdata())
smeared_new_colors = len(set(big_bilinear.getdata()) - source_colors)
nonuniform = 0
for y in range(base.height):
    for x in range(base.width):
        block = big_bilinear.crop((x * cs.ZOOM, y * cs.ZOOM,
                                   (x + 1) * cs.ZOOM, (y + 1) * cs.ZOOM))
        distinct = set(block.getdata())
        if len(distinct) != 1 or distinct.pop() != base.getpixel((x, y)):
            nonuniform += 1
sampling_discriminates = smeared_new_colors > 0 and nonuniform > 0
ok_overall &= sampling_discriminates
report["sampling_negative_control"] = {
    "description": "Same art enlarged 8x with BILINEAR instead of NEAREST.",
    "new_colors_introduced": smeared_new_colors,
    "nonuniform_blocks": nonuniform,
    "discriminates": sampling_discriminates,
}

report["result"] = "pass" if ok_overall else "fail"
report["limits"] = [
    "This proves the checking code discriminates on controlled mutants.",
    "It is not a PixelLab generation, not a candidate for f.sprite, and not evidence "
    "about the artistic quality of any sprite.",
    "q.identity and q.webdisplay are untouched by this proof.",
]
path = ROOT / "work" / "poc" / "harness-proof.json"
path.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True), encoding="utf-8")
print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in report.items() if k != "cases"}, indent=2))
for case in report["cases"]:
    print(case["name"], "expected", case["expected_failures"],
          "actual", case["actual_failures"], "->", case["as_predicted"])
sys.exit(0 if ok_overall else 1)

"""Acceptance harness for the teal scout robot sample.

Runs the locally decidable criteria declared in .pixl/state.px against a candidate PNG
and writes a JSON receipt plus a contact sheet for the visual criterion.

    python tools/check_sprite.py CANDIDATE.png --out work/receipt.json \
        --sheet work/contact-sheet.png

Criteria implemented here:
  q.canvas   mechanical  single 32x32 frame
  q.palette  mechanical  zero pixels outside #25354A / #56B5BC / #F4DDA2
  q.alpha    mechanical  zero fractional-alpha pixels
  q.nearest  other       8x nearest enlargement adds no colour and tiles uniformly

q.identity (visual) and q.webdisplay (engine) are NOT decided here. This script only
renders the contact sheet an agent or person must actually look at, and reports the
measurements that support -- but cannot replace -- that judgement.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import pathlib
import sys
from collections import Counter

from PIL import Image

PALETTE = ["#25354A", "#56B5BC", "#F4DDA2"]
SIZE = (32, 32)
ZOOM = 8


def rgba(hex_color):
    value = hex_color.lstrip("#")
    return tuple(int(value[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4)) + (255,)


ALLOWED = {rgba(c) for c in PALETTE}


def load_frames(path):
    with Image.open(path) as image:
        count = getattr(image, "n_frames", 1)
        frames = []
        for index in range(count):
            image.seek(index)
            frames.append(image.convert("RGBA").copy())
    return frames


def visible(frame):
    return [p for p in frame.getdata() if p[3] != 0]


def check_canvas(frames):
    sizes = [f.size for f in frames]
    ok = len(frames) == 1 and sizes[0] == SIZE
    return ok, {"frame_count": len(frames), "sizes": [list(s) for s in sizes],
                "required": [list(SIZE), "single frame"]}


def check_palette(frame):
    counts = Counter(visible(frame))
    outside = sorted(c for c in counts if c not in ALLOWED)
    ok = not outside
    return ok, {
        "visible_colors": len(counts),
        "outside_palette_count": len(outside),
        "outside_palette": ["#%02X%02X%02X (alpha %d)" % (c[0], c[1], c[2], c[3])
                            for c in outside[:16]],
        "counts": {"#%02X%02X%02X" % c[:3]: n for c, n in counts.most_common()},
    }


def check_alpha(frame):
    alphas = Counter(p[3] for p in frame.getdata())
    fractional = sum(n for a, n in alphas.items() if a not in (0, 255))
    return fractional == 0, {"fractional_alpha_pixels": fractional,
                             "alpha_levels": sorted(alphas)}


def check_nearest(frame, zoom=ZOOM):
    """Integer nearest enlargement must add no colour and tile uniformly."""
    big = frame.resize((frame.width * zoom, frame.height * zoom), Image.NEAREST)
    source_colors = set(frame.getdata())
    new_colors = sorted(set(big.getdata()) - source_colors)
    ragged = []
    for y in range(frame.height):
        for x in range(frame.width):
            block = big.crop((x * zoom, y * zoom, (x + 1) * zoom, (y + 1) * zoom))
            distinct = set(block.getdata())
            if len(distinct) != 1 or distinct.pop() != frame.getpixel((x, y)):
                ragged.append([x, y])
    ok = not new_colors and not ragged
    return ok, {"zoom": zoom, "new_colors": len(new_colors),
                "nonuniform_blocks": len(ragged), "first_nonuniform": ragged[:8]}


def checkerboard(size, cell=8):
    board = Image.new("RGBA", size, (255, 255, 255, 255))
    for y in range(0, size[1], cell):
        for x in range(0, size[0], cell):
            if (x // cell + y // cell) % 2:
                board.paste((203, 203, 203, 255), (x, y, min(x + cell, size[0]),
                                                   min(y + cell, size[1])))
    return board


def contact_sheet(candidate, reference, path):
    """Reference and candidate at 8x over light, dark and checker backgrounds,
    plus both at native 32x32, in one image to be looked at."""
    pad, zoom = 8, ZOOM
    tile = 32 * zoom
    backgrounds = [("light", (245, 245, 245, 255)), ("dark", (18, 18, 18, 255)),
                   ("checker", None)]
    cols, rows = 2, len(backgrounds)
    width = pad + cols * (tile + pad)
    height = pad + rows * (tile + pad) + 32 + pad * 2
    sheet = Image.new("RGBA", (width, height), (128, 128, 128, 255))
    for row, (_, color) in enumerate(backgrounds):
        y = pad + row * (tile + pad)
        for col, image in enumerate((reference, candidate)):
            x = pad + col * (tile + pad)
            back = (checkerboard((tile, tile)) if color is None
                    else Image.new("RGBA", (tile, tile), color))
            back.alpha_composite(image.resize((tile, tile), Image.NEAREST))
            sheet.paste(back, (x, y))
    y = pad + rows * (tile + pad)
    for col, image in enumerate((reference, candidate)):
        back = Image.new("RGBA", (32, 32), (245, 245, 245, 255))
        back.alpha_composite(image)
        sheet.paste(back, (pad + col * (tile + pad), y))
    sheet.save(path)
    return path


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("candidate")
    parser.add_argument("--reference", default="reference.png")
    parser.add_argument("--out")
    parser.add_argument("--sheet")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    frames = load_frames(args.candidate)
    frame = frames[0]
    results = {}
    results["q.canvas"] = check_canvas(frames)
    results["q.palette"] = check_palette(frame)
    results["q.alpha"] = check_alpha(frame)
    results["q.nearest"] = check_nearest(frame)

    receipt = {
        "candidate": args.candidate,
        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(args.candidate).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        "contract": {"px": list(SIZE), "pl": PALETTE, "al": "binary", "sa": "nearest"},
        "criteria": {k: {"outcome": "pass" if ok else "fail", "measurements": data}
                     for k, (ok, data) in results.items()},
        "not_decided_here": {
            "q.identity": "visual criterion; requires actually viewing the contact sheet",
            "q.webdisplay": "engine criterion; requires the owner's web prototype",
        },
    }
    if args.sheet:
        reference = load_frames(args.reference)[0]
        receipt["contact_sheet"] = contact_sheet(frame, reference, args.sheet)
    text = json.dumps(receipt, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    if args.out:
        pathlib.Path(args.out).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    print(text)
    return 0 if all(ok for ok, _ in results.values()) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Draft PixelLab request for f.sprite

Recorded 2026-09-11 by PIXL. **This is a draft, not saved provider intent.** No `J` record
exists in `.pixl/state.px`, because `job-prepare` requires the exact `inputSchema` observed
from a connected PixelLab server, and no such server is connected in this session
(see `pixellab-discovery.md`). Saving this text as a prepared request would fabricate a
discovery observation, which the provider operation forbids.

When a PixelLab MCP server is connected, the operator should re-run discovery, read the
actual tool list and `inputSchema`, adjust the argument names below to match what the
schema really accepts, and only then run `job-prepare` / `job-dispatch`.

## Tool selection (to be re-confirmed against the live schema)

The dated documentation snapshot lists several generation entry points. Ranked for this
task:

1. **`create_image_pixflux` / `create_image_pixen`** — documented as requiring
   `description`, polled with `get_image`. A direct single-image generator is the closest
   match for one 32x32 still at a fixed size.
2. **`create_character`** — documented as requiring `description`, polled with
   `get_character`. Preferable only if the later family expansion turns out to be
   animation or directional states, because a character resource carries those forward.
3. **`image_to_pixelart`** — only relevant if the operator would rather supply a
   higher-resolution source image than a text description.

`i.family_scope` is unresolved, so the choice between 1 and 2 cannot be settled yet. If the
owner's family is poses or directions of this same robot, option 2 avoids regenerating the
identity for every member.

## Description to send

> 32x32 pixel art sprite of a small teal scout robot, side view, standing upright.
> Rectangular boxy body, flat teal #56B5BC fill with no shading, gradients or dithering.
> Uniform dark navy #25354A outline around the whole silhouette. Two straight antennae
> rising from the top of the head, drawn in the same dark navy as the outline, with a gap
> between them. Two pale yellow #F4DDA2 rectangular eyes, both visible, no pupils, no eye
> outline. Exactly three colours total. Fully transparent background, hard edges, no
> anti-aliasing, no ground shadow, no drop shadow, no floor or contact shading, no
> background scenery.

## Parameters to set if the live schema exposes them

| Intent | Parameter to look for | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canvas | `image_size` / `width` + `height` | 32 x 32 |
| Style reference | `style_image` / `init_image` / `reference` | `reference.png` |
| Palette lock | `forced_palette` / `palette` / `color_palette` | `#25354A`, `#56B5BC`, `#F4DDA2` |
| Outline policy | `outline` | a single hard dark outline |
| Shading policy | `shading` / `detail` | flat, no shading |
| View | `view` / `camera` | side |
| Transparency | `transparent` / `no_background` | on |

## Requirements the tool may not be able to express

State these in the prepared request so the acceptance step knows what is untested at
submission time:

- **Exact three-colour palette.** If no palette parameter exists, the returned PNG will
  almost certainly carry extra anti-aliasing and shading colours. `q.palette` will fail and
  the candidate must be revised or quantised with a follow-up tool (the snapshot documents
  `reduce_colors` and `correct_pixelart` for this) rather than accepted.
- **Binary alpha.** Generators commonly return soft alpha at the silhouette edge.
  `q.alpha` will catch it.
- **Two eyes in a side view.** `i.eye_presentation` is only a proposal. A returned profile
  head with one eye fails `q.identity` and must be reported to the owner rather than
  silently accepted.
- **No ground shadow.** Frequently added by default; `q.identity` checks for it visually
  and the connected-component count in the harness receipt helps spot a detached blob.

## After a returned asset

1. Download into the project, then `job-import` to snapshot the bytes as a candidate of
   `f.sprite`.
2. `python tools/check_sprite.py <candidate> --out work/receipt.json --sheet work/sheet.png`
   for `q.canvas`, `q.palette`, `q.alpha` and `q.nearest`.
3. Actually look at `work/sheet.png` and record `q.identity` as pass or fail.
4. `q.webdisplay` stays unavailable until `i.web_prototype` is resolved.
